# ManateeCreekSystems: what it can do, and how it got here

The one-page public website for Manatee Creek Systems LLC (manateecreeksystems.com), served as static files from a single index.html.

## How we got here

Every change entry, newest first: what it was for, and what it made possible.

### 20261125-self-hosted-libertinus

Task `kanon-rename-20261125`.

**Why.** Visitors' own Apple and Microsoft fonts, and a Palatino clone in the share image, left the site's lettering resting on fonts we do not license; Ken wants fonts nobody can sue over.

**Enables.** The site and its share image use Libertinus Serif under the SIL Open Font License, served from the site itself with no request to Google or any font service.

**Untested:** Font swap with no test suite here; verified in Chromium that the font loads from the site, no font request leaves it, and the page still fits a phone.

### 20261125-kanon-rename

Task `kanon-rename-20261125`.

**Why.** The product name Sophos raised a copyright concern, so the public site must stop presenting it under that name.

**Enables.** Visitors, search engines and social previews see the product as Kanon, with a matching Greek gloss and share image, so the site can be shared without the old name.

**Untested:** Static copy and image change with no test suite in this repo; verified by rendering the page in Chromium and confirming no visible Sophos text remains.

### 20261119-state-machines-skill

Task `state-machines-skill-20261119`.

**Why.** Ken asked for the implicit-state-machine question to be part of Sophos and called upon every time we code, in every household repo.

**Enables.** This repo carries the synced state-machines skill and the Sophos front door 1.4.3, which names it: on every coding task, check the code being touched for an implicit state machine and make the change that lifts UX, DX and AX without breaking anything.

**Untested:** skill text only; both files byte-identical to their sources (Project-Sophos skills/state-machines/SKILL.md and open-claw-stuff skills/sophos/SKILL.md), synced by tools/skill-sync; the hook and its tests live in Project-Sophos

### 20261109-skill-sync-four-questions

Task `ocs-mirror-four-questions-20261109`.

**Why.** The four-questions skill changed at its source (Project-Sophos@960ef7be0dbf) and this copy is declared synced.

**Enables.** This repository carries the current four-questions skill, byte-identical to its source.

**Untested:** a mirrored skill file; skill-sync verified it byte-identical to the source before staging

### 20261031-sophos-skill-1-4-2

Task `skill-sync-sophos-1-4-2-argus-mcs-20261031`.

**Why.** ManateeCreekSystems held the sophos skill at v1.4.1, missing the 23-line re-bootstrap block that tells an agent to redo the whole bootstrap when it expires, so an agent here would not be told to.

**Enables.** An agent working in this repo is told the same expiry rule as every other household repo, and skill-sync reports this repo in sync with the source instead of one version behind.

**Untested:** A copy of one skill file from its source; the bytes were compared by sha256 against Project-Sophos main and the copy loses nothing, since its only exclusive line was the version line.

### 20261028-change-record-in-manateecreeksystems

Task `change-record-deploy-repos-20261028`.

**Why.** ManateeCreekSystems had no record of why its code changes: a commit message keeps what changed, not why it mattered, and the reason lived only in the memory of whoever made it. Ken asked on 2026-10-27 for the household change record in every repository, tuned to each.

**Enables.** Every commit that changes the one-page site now carries why it mattered and what it enables, judged when it is made; the page mixes copy, style and behaviour, so every change to it is judged.

**Untested:** This commit installs the gate here; the engine and this repository's tuning are tested in Project-Sophos, in admin/tests/change-record.test.mjs and admin/tests/change-record-deploy.test.mjs.
